Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the Nexara Cloud Q2 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, we will conduct a question-and-answer session. If you would like to ask a question at that time, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us. Today, we will be discussing Nexara Cloud's results for the Q2 FY2024. With me on the call are Jordan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; Marcus Lee, Chief Product Officer; Lisa Wong, Chief Marketing Officer; Tom Reilly, Chief Sales Officer; and Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Security Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call contains forward-looking statements. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Hale.

Jordan Hale:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. Nexara Cloud continued its strong growth trajectory in the Q2, driven by robust demand for our comprehensive suite of cloud services and solutions.

During the quarter, our key priorities included:
1. Expanding our presence in emerging markets.
2. Accelerating the adoption of our AI-powered platform.
3. Enhancing our developer ecosystem.
4. Strengthening our commitment to sustainability.
5. Investing in employee training and development.
6. Improving cross-functional collaboration.
7. Ensuring the security and privacy of our customers' data.

Let me dive deeper into our geographic revenue performance, which really highlights the global scalability of our cloud platform. In Q2 FY2024, we achieved total revenue of $28.7 billion, marking a 19% increase year-over-year and 8% quarter-over-quarter, propelled by strong demand across our core IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS offerings, especially in high-performance computing for generative AI workloads and data analytics.

Breaking it down by our standard regions—Americas, which covers primarily the U.S. and Canada with growing Latin America contributions; EMEA, spanning Europe, Middle East, and Africa; and APAC, Asia-Pacific—our mix shows the strength of our mature U.S. enterprise customer base alongside accelerating international expansion. International revenue now makes up 42% of the total, up from 38% a year ago.

In the Americas, we generated $15.8 billion, or 55% of total revenue. This grew 15% year-over-year and 6% quarter-over-quarter, with some normalization from hyperscale customer ramps compared to Q1's 17% growth, but still powered by deep penetration among Fortune 500 companies. U.S. revenue hit $14.9 billion, up 16% year-over-year, thanks to strong performance from our Nitro Enclaves for confidential computing and SageMaker-like integrations enabling large-scale AI model training, similar to workloads for partners like those akin to OpenAI or Anthropic. Latin America added $0.9 billion, surging 35% year-over-year, boosted by our new São Paulo Region 2 data center, which launched last quarter and is running at 75% utilization. Wins include sovereign cloud for Brazilian financial services under LGPD data residency and edge computing with telecoms like Claro for 5G slicing. Remaining performance obligations, or RPO, in the Americas rose 22% year-over-year to $112 billion, pointing to multi-year AI infrastructure commitments.

EMEA delivered $6.2 billion, 22% of total revenue, our fastest-growing area at 28% year-over-year and 12% quarter-over-quarter, outpacing the company average for three straight quarters. Europe contributed $5.1 billion, up 30% year-over-year, driven by GDPR-compliant solutions like our EU Sovereign Cloud in Frankfurt and Paris, which booked 40% sequential capacity. Regulated sectors like healthcare with federated learning pilots similar to NHS and automotive ADAS training using Inferentia-like chips with OEMs like BMW are key. Middle East and Africa added $1.1 billion, up 22%, led by UAE and Saudi Arabia after our Dammam region launch, tailored for oil and gas HPC on Graviton4 Arm-based instances. Sustainability helps here—carbon-free energy matching in Nordic zones has secured hyperscaler deals, replacing on-prem. EMEA RPO reached $48 billion, up 32% year-over-year, with multi-cloud via Outposts-like service ensuring hybrid stickiness.

APAC brought in $5.7 billion, or 20% including other at 3%, with 26% year-over-year and 11% quarter-over-quarter growth, reflecting rapid cloud adoption in digital transformations. Japan and Australia combined for $2.4 billion, up 24%, supported by Tokyo Region 3 for yen-based AI services with SoftBank and NTT Docomo. India jumped to $1.2 billion, 45% growth, via Mumbai's data centers and Bedrock-like GenAI capturing 30% public sector share, partnering with Reliance Jio on edge AI. China-excluding APAC like Singapore and Korea added $1.6 billion, up 25%, handling localization with compliant zones. Other areas rounded out at $0.8 billion. APAC RPO climbed 38% to $42 billion, with hyperscale and telco 5G trends.

Over the last four quarters, international growth has doubled the Americas pace: EMEA at 27% CAGR, APAC 29% versus Americas 16%. This diversification reduces U.S. macro risks, like Big Tech capex moderation—our top 10 hyperscalers grew 25% but SMBs and enterprises outpaced. We're investing $10 billion in FY2024 capex for 12 new Availability Zones, 40% APAC, 30% EMEA, featuring Global Accelerator for low-latency AI and Trainium2 clusters with 40% better TCO than Nvidia GPUs. Sovereign clouds meet 60+ regulations, Direct Connect with 500+ partners builds ecosystems. For Q3, expect international at 30%+ year-over-year, APAC nearing 30% mix by FY2025, GenAI at 15% pipeline, edge-to-cloud. Gross margins over 95% hold, international OpEx efficiencies add 200 basis points.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen to discuss our financial performance in more detail.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Jordan. We are pleased to report another quarter of strong financial results. Revenue grew by 19% year-over-year to $28.7 billion, exceeding our guidance. Our gross margin was 78%, reflecting our efficient cost structure. Our operating margin was 28%.

As we close out a record quarter with that robust growth, let me highlight our energy efficiency and sustainability initiatives, a key competitive advantage in an industry where data centers use 2-3% of global electricity, projected to 1,000 TWh by 2026 per IEA. This isn't just ESG—it's margin expansion, retention, and compliance, saving us over $650 million YTD in energy costs, adding 120 basis points to non-GAAP operating margin, leading peers in Uptime Institute and Green Grid benchmarks.

Our global PUE improved to 1.12 in Q2, from 1.18 year-end 2022, 25% better than industry 1.50 average, matching Google's 1.10 with more AI capacity. Cooling overhead dropped 32% via retrofits in 45 regions. Renewables hit 105% matching YTD, procuring 1.2 million MWh extra CFE, exceeding RE100. WUE fell 18% to 0.22 liters/kWh with closed-loop cooling, better than Azure's 0.25. 82% of top 500 enterprises like PharmaGiant and Unilever factor sustainability in RFPs, adding 5-7% premiums; Scope 3 demand up 40% under EU CSRD and California SB 253.

Technically, AI-driven orchestration via Nexus Optimizer uses reinforcement learning for 22% savings on H100 clusters across 250,000 GPUs in Virginia, Frankfurt, Singapore. 60% new capacity has direct-to-chip liquid cooling, 40% less energy; Graviton4 and TPU v5e give 2.7x perf/watt, 35% less watts/TOPS. Free-air cooling in 70% sites, DVFS, sodium-ion batteries cut Scope 3 15%. Capex efficiency $0.45 per revenue run-rate vs. peers $0.55.

Regionally: North America (55% capacity) 115% renewables via NextEra, Ørsted PPAs, eyeing SMRs for 20% US by 2026. EMEA (25%) sub-1.10 PUE in Frankfurt/Paris, EU Taxonomy; Sweden 99.9% CFE. APAC (20%) Singapore wind, Tokyo hydrogen; India solar PPAs cut carbon 28%. Saudi NEOM 100% solar.

This drives 15-20% customer TCO cuts amid $200B AI capex. Each 0.01 PUE saves $45M annually. We lead AWS 90% renewables, Azure WUE. Ahead: $4.2B green capex for 1.08 PUE, 120% matching, net-zero Scope 1&2 by 2030, Scope 3 roadmaps. Quarterly CDP CFE hours, Nexara Green Reservations at 3% premium, backlogged. Cumulative $1B+ savings, growth in 20% CAGR market.

Next, I'd like to introduce Dr. Elena Vasquez, who will provide an update on our technology roadmap.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Sarah. We are making significant investments in research and development to stay at the forefront of cloud innovation. We are particularly excited about our progress in AI-powered platforms.

Good afternoon, everyone. Today, I'll cover our new customer acquisition cost, or CAC, analysis—a vital metric for sales efficiency and scalable profitability in our model, where LTV exceeds $5 million over five years for enterprises. Optimizing CAC boosts LTV/CAC, payback, and magic number for sales/marketing efficiency.

In Q2 FY24, blended CAC was $42,500, down 19% year-over-year from $52,300 and 5% sequentially from $44,700—six quarters of compression via productivity, product-led growth, partners. Beats Gartner median $55-65k for peers.

By segment: Enterprise (> $1M ARR) $138,000, down 22% from $177,000, shorter 4.2-month cycles vs. 6.1 via ABM for Fortune 1000 VMware to Nexara Kubernetes Service migrations. Mid-market ($100k-$1M) $28,400, down 3%, inbound from developer portal, 28% conversion on free-tier Nexara Functions. SMB $4,200 flat, 15% higher volume via marketplaces.

Regions: North America (58% new logos) $38,900 lowest, Accenture/Deloitte channels 42% wins, 2.3 deals/rep/quarter, 11-month payback. EMEA $46,200 down 17%, GDPR storage wins like BNP Paribas. APAC $52,800 slight rise on ramps, but 37% ARR growth, sovereign Tokyo/Mumbai, co-sell AWS/Azure.

Payback 12.4 months blended from 15.2, elite vs. Snowflake 14-16. LTV/CAC 4.8x on 125% NRR, SageCore AI 300% attach.

Drivers: AI sales tools (Gong, 6sense) 24% conversion lift; PLG 35% ARR self-serve, freemium AI Studio viral; channels 51% deals, 1,200+ Marketplace ISVs cut burn 28%; macro TCO 35% vs. VMware, $15M retailer migration.

Q3-Q4: 15-20% compression, 22% revenue S&M down from 27%. Levers: AI personalization 50k accounts, $50M APAC/LatAm, NVIDIA sovereign AI for $200B market.

Validates flywheel: lower CAC, faster payback, higher LTV for 25%+ FCF margins FY25.

Now, I'll pass it to Marcus Lee for a product update.

Marcus Lee:
Thank you, Elena. We recently launched Nexara AI Foundry, which is already gaining significant traction in the market.

Thank you, everyone, for joining our Q2 call. I'm Marcus Lee, and I'll outline key assumptions for our FY24 and FY25 revenue and profitability forecasts. As a hyperscale leader powering 45,000+ customers with IaaS, Kubernetes Engine, AI Inference, we project $28.5 billion FY24 (28% YoY), $36.2 billion FY25 (27% YoY), EBITDA margins 32% then 35%.

Assumptions span macro, customer, product, competitive, ops—forward-looking with risks like volatility, AI supply, competition.

Revenue: 72% consumption, NRR 128% FY24/132% FY25, Q2 cohorts +35% on migrations/AI.

1. AI/ML 45% growth: $12.8B FY24 (85% YoY), 45% mix. GPU util >85%, A100/H100/Blackwell ramps like OpenAI betas. AI Fabric InfiniBand cuts training 40%; 60% inference serverless. Hedge GPU shortages with AMD MI300X.

2. Modernization/multi-cloud 30%: 22% adoption CAGR, 65% top customers hybrid. IaaS/PaaS $18.2B +25%, VM 30%, NKE 40%, ACV $4.2M. SaaS/analytics $6.1B +20%.

3. Regions: NA 55% +24%, 12 regions 90% util. EMEA 20% +35%, sovereign €50B public. APAC 18% +42%, India/SEA 5G $2.5B RPO. LatAm 7% +28%.

4. Customers: Churn <4%, expansions 118-140% NRR, 15k net new, RPO $42B +33%. AI Everywhere 25% attach.

Profitability: Op margins 28% FY24 (+400bps)/32% FY25, FCF $9.2B 32%.

Gross 78.5%: Util 82% (PUE 1.18 liquid), no discounts, AI premium, Graviton3 35% compute saves.

OpEx 42%: R&D 12% $3.4B quantum crypto/800GbE/carbon-free FY26. S&M 18% CAC <9mo 60% partners. G&A 5% headcount +18% to 92k.

CapEx $14.5B 51% rev, dep 4yr GPUs, falls 42% FY25.

Risks: Price wars 100bps, slowdown 2-3%, 70% recurring resilience. Validated $52B RPO, 135% NRR Q2.

I'll now hand it over to Lisa Wong to discuss our marketing strategy.

Lisa Wong:
Thank you, Marcus. Our marketing efforts are focused on building brand awareness and generating demand for our solutions.

Good afternoon. In Q2 FY2024, compute utilization hit 84% overall, up 300bps QoQ from 81%, 650bps YoY from 77.5%, across 5M vCPUs. x86/ARM 82%, GPUs 92% for GenAI training/inference like GPT/Llama. Storage 93% aggregate, +200bps QoQ/800bps YoY, hot object 95%, block 89%.

Outperforms AWS mid-80s, Azure 82%. Nexara Optimizer ML rightsizing cuts overprovision 25%.

Regions: NA 52% rev, compute 87%, storage 94%, hyperscalers Salesforce/Adobe to NKS. EMEA compute 81%/storage 91%, sovereign Frankfurt/Paris confidential AI. APAC compute 88%/95%, SoftBank Arm AI, Mumbai spot.

Drivers: GenAI GPU +150%, Zero Egress AWS migrations 35%, ESG PUE 1.18 65% renewables.

Initiatives: Dynamic Capacity Orchestrator RL +12% util, RI 62%, tiered storage reclaims 8%. $4.2B CapEx 40% GPU Virginia/Ohio/Osaka, ROIC >25%.

Q3 guide 85-87% compute/93-95% storage, upside AI Foundry +500bps GPU. Risks Blackwell delays, diversified TSMC/Intel.

Next, I'd like to introduce Tom Reilly, who will provide an update on our sales performance.

Tom Reilly:
Thank you, Lisa. Our sales team delivered a strong performance in the Q2, driven by increased customer adoption of our cloud services.

Good afternoon. Before guidance, our network performance/reliability: FY24 on track for 99.999% uptime, exceeding 99.99% SLA, 100% credits, +0.0003pp QoQ, ~26min less downtime YoY. p99 latency 68ms global -12% YoY for AV/HFT. Backbone 450+ PoPs 200Tbps, RTT -15% inter-region, BGP/ peering Level3/Zayo.

Throughput 45EB egress Q2 +32% YoY, 99.97% line rate, loss 0.008%<0.01%, retrans 0.12%, MTBF 1.2M hrs, MTTR <4min vs AWS 5.2.

Regions: Americas 52% p95 12ms intra N.Virginia, 65ms cross, MAREA 400Gbps AI NVIDIA. EMEA 28% 99.998% uptime, Frankfurt/Paris <25ms p99, DDoS 2.5Tbps zero impact Radware. APAC 20% intra 18ms Singapore/Tokyo SJC2, cross-India 85ms, new Mumbai/Jakarta PoPs sub-50ms 5G.

Initiatives: AetherNet AI preempts 92% anomalies -35% MTTR, re-routes. +50Tbps 800G Ciena to 250Tbps, $2.5B FY25 transpacific Meta/MSFT FarEast. Edge 250 cities -40% last-mile, Outposts/Azure Stack hybrids.

NRR 128% GenAI 3x inference, high-SLA 65% bookings +13pp. $8B capex 18% network quantum/terabit 6G. Growth engine for $800B TAM sub-50ms sovereign AI.

Finally, I'll pass it to Dr. Raj Patel to discuss our security initiatives.

Dr. Raj Patel:
Thank you, Tom. Security is our top priority. We are committed to protecting our customers' data and maintaining the highest standards of security.

Thank you, Jordan, and good afternoon. On capex outlook: focused on AI, storage, sovereign for 22% CAGR to $1T TAM by FY27.

FY24 $28.4B +18% YoY: data centers $17.2B 60% AI Fabric H100/Blackwell TPUs; servers $6.8B 24%; network/edge $2.9B 10%.

FY25 $34-36B +20-25% mid, Q1 $8.2-8.5B to Q4 $9.5-10B; FY26 $40-42B on AI. Capex/rev 28-30% from 32%, util 85% 45 regions.

Data centers 62% $21-22B, 12 new 2.5GW: $8B GPU/liquid H200/B200/MI300X DynamoAI; $1.2B renewables PUE<1.15 70% FY26 carbon-neutral 2030.

Servers/compute $8.5B 24%, Nitro 3nm 30% instances +25% perf, $500M enclaves SGX/SEV-SNP.

Network/edge $3.5B +20%, 400Gbps Broadcom 15 metro, Verizon/Vodafone AR/AV.

Regions: NA 45% $15.5-16B Ashburn+500MW Texas/Oregon gas/colos. EMEA 25% $8.5-9B Frankfurt-3/Paris-2/UK London-4 GDPR +8pp share. APAC 20% $7-7.5B Mumbai-2/Osaka-3 China JV $1B SEA. LATAM/Other 10% $3.5B São Paulo-2 Riyadh/Dubai.

ROI 3-4x 24mo 90% contracted, Interconnect -30% egress. Risks supply/power/inflation, AI planning optimizes $1.2B.

Owns AI era: 100+ regions, inference economics, sustainability moat, 25%+ growth/margins.

Back to Jordan Hale.

Jordan Hale:
Thank you, everyone. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, at this time we will begin the question-and-answer session. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Ben Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Ben Smith:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Jordan, can you elaborate on the drivers behind the accelerating international growth, particularly in APAC and EMEA, and how that factors into your long-term mix?

Jordan Hale:
Thanks, Ben. Absolutely, as I detailed earlier, EMEA's 28% growth and APAC's 26% reflect sovereign cloud traction and GenAI tailwinds. We're prioritizing capex there—40% APAC, 30% EMEA—for 30%+ Q3 international acceleration, aiming APAC at 30% mix by FY25. Diversification strengthens resilience.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Priya Patel with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Priya Patel:
Great, thanks. Sarah, with capex ramping to $34-36 billion next year, how do you think about margins and FCF conversion, especially with AI intensity?

Sarah Chen:
Hi Priya. Margins expand to 32% FY25 via 82%+ utilization, PUE improvements, and OpEx discipline—S&M down to 22% revenue. FCF hits 32% on recurring 70% revenue, ROI 3-4x on capex. AI drives it, balanced by efficiencies like Graviton silicon.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Kim with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Kim:
Thanks. Elena, on the tech side, with GPU util at 92%, what's the roadmap for next-gen like Blackwell and how does network support low-latency AI?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
David, great question. Blackwell ramps H1 FY25 with 150k units, paired with AI Fabric InfiniBand for 40% faster training. Network p99 68ms, AetherNet AI preempts issues, edge expansions sub-50ms for inference—powers 3x faster GenAI, key to 85% NRR.

Jordan Hale:
Thank you for your questions. We appreciate your continued support.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the call.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
